new.md:
Creates a new color button.

This returns a widget in the form of a small button containing
a swatch representing the current selected color. When the button
is clicked, a color chooser dialog will open, allowing the user
to select a color. The swatch will be updated to reflect the new
color when the user finishes.

new_with_rgba.brief: Creates a new color button showing the given color.
new_with_rgba.md: Creates a new color button showing the given color.

doc.brief: The `GtkColorButton` allows to open a color chooser dialog to change the color.
doc.md:
The `GtkColorButton` allows to open a color chooser dialog to change
the color.

It is suitable widget for selecting a color in a preference dialog.

# CSS nodes

```
colorbutton
╰── button.color
    ╰── [content]
```

`GtkColorButton` has a single CSS node with name colorbutton which
contains a button node. To differentiate it from a plain `GtkButton`,
it gets the .color style class.

show-editor.brief: Whether the color chooser should open in editor mode.
show-editor.md:
Whether the color chooser should open in editor mode.

This property should be used in cases where the palette
in the editor would be redundant, such as when the color
button is already part of a palette.

activate.brief: Emitted to when the color button is activated.
activate.md:
Emitted to when the color button is activated.

The `::activate` signal on `GtkMenuButton` is an action signal and
emitting it causes the button to pop up its dialog.

color-set.brief: Emitted when the user selects a color.
color-set.md:
Emitted when the user selects a color.

When handling this signal, use [`ColorChooser.get_rgba()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColorChooser#method:get_rgba)
to find out which color was just selected.

Note that this signal is only emitted when the user changes the color.
If you need to react to programmatic color changes as well, use
the notify::rgba signal.
